request.description: I, Pencil: a pencil supply chain that keeps running. Loggers cut cedar in Oregon, a mill saws it into slats, graphite is mined in Sri Lanka and mixed with clay into leads, a factory in Pennsylvania glues leads into slats, paints them and adds erasers and brass ferrules, packs them into boxes, and trucks deliver the boxes to shops across the country, which sell them to customers.

second_source_processes: renew-cedar-stock adds stock.logs (already added from nothing by cut-cedar)
renew-graphite-stock adds stock.graphite (already added from nothing by mine-graphite)

world.label: Pencil Supply Chain
world.summary: A continuing supply chain makes, ships, and sells pencils from raw materials to customers.

actions.description: Cut cedar logs for the sawmill.
The sawmill buys cedar logs from the logging business.
Saw cedar logs into pencil slats.
Carry slats from the sawmill to the pencil factory.
Mine graphite for pencil leads.
The lead works buys graphite from the mine.
The lead works buys clay from its supplier.
Mix graphite with clay and form pencil leads.
Carry leads from the lead works to the pencil factory.
Glue leads into slats, paint the pencils, and attach erasers and brass ferrules.
Pack finished pencils into boxes.
Carry boxed pencils from the factory to the shop for sale.
Sell boxed pencils to customers.

readout.title: How goods moved through the chain
readout.summary: The logger supplied logs, the sawmill turned logs into slats, and the lead-works made leads from clay and graphite. The carrier moved slats and leads to the pencil factory, which made and packed pencils, but the recorded events do not show pencils reaching the shop or customers taking them.
